title: The poem's images
back: Shed, polished traffic, city money, the open window, the good-doers, the poet.

title: The poem's movement
back: Shed → traffic passes → why they stop → childish longing → good-doers → the poet's pain.

title: The open window
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="The childish longing in vain" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><rect x="100" y="40" width="120" height="120" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="6"/><path d="M160,40 V160 M100,100 H220" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><g><circle cx="140" cy="104.6" r="6.6" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.6" stroke="none"/><path d="M131.0,119.19999999999999 Q140,111.19999999999999 149.0,119.19999999999999 L156.2,158 H123.8 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.6" stroke="none"/></g><text x="160" y="185" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">waiting for the squeal of brakes</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">The childish longing in vain</text></svg>
back: All day the farmers wait for a car to slow, a hand with money. Frost calls it childish — innocent and unrealistic — and can hardly bear it.

title: Greedy good-doers
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Beneficent beasts of prey — help that destroys independence" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><g><circle cx="100" cy="73.2" r="13.2" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><path d="M82.0,94.4 Q100,86.4 118.0,94.4 L115.12,129.6 L107.2,129.6 L108.64,180 H101.8 L100.72,132.0 H99.28 L98.2,180 H91.36 L92.8,129.6 L84.88,129.6 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><path d="M80.2,66.60000000000001 H119.8 V61.32000000000001 H111.88 V46.800000000000004 H88.12 V61.32000000000001 H80.2 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/></g><g><circle cx="200" cy="126.6" r="6.6" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.4" stroke="none"/><path d="M191.0,141.2 Q200,133.2 209.0,141.2 L207.56,154.8 L203.6,154.8 L204.32,180 H200.9 L200.36,156.0 H199.64 L199.1,180 H195.68 L196.4,154.8 L192.44,154.8 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.4" stroke="none"/></g><path d="M130,110 L180,120 M170.5,123.0 L180,120 L172.3,113.6" fill="none" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><rect x="230" y="100" width="60" height="50" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none" rx="4"/><text x="260" y="130" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none">theatre</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Beneficent beasts of prey — help that destroys independence</text></svg>
back: Oxymorons for false philanthropy: relocate the poor near the theatre and store, teach them to sleep all day, soothe them out of their wits.

title: Would I accept such mercy?
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="The poet turns his cruel 'kindness' on himself" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><g><circle cx="160" cy="73.2" r="13.2" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><path d="M142.0,94.4 Q160,86.4 178.0,94.4 L175.12,129.6 L167.2,129.6 L168.64,180 H161.8 L160.72,132.0 H159.28 L158.2,180 H151.36 L152.8,129.6 L144.88,129.6 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/></g><path d="M110,70 Q160,20 210,70" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="4 4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><circle cx="160" cy="40" r="10" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">The poet turns his cruel 'kindness' on himself</text></svg>
back: He thinks of ending their pain at one stroke, then asks how he would feel if someone offered him that. Irony and honesty: pity is easy from a passing car.

title: The phrase to recognise
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Line to remember" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><g><rect x="28" y="36" width="264" height="72" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.08" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" rx="10"/><path d="M50,108 L42,122 L64,108 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><text x="160.0" y="78.3" text-anchor="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">the flower of cities</text></g><text x="160" y="146" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.8" stroke="none">— what the farmers want a share of</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Line to remember</text></svg>
back: Urban prosperity, the good life the newspapers and films promise. The farmers are not begging; they want to feel it too.
